key_insight: Autoregressive Boltzmann Generators replace flow-based sampling with autoregressive modeling, enabling more expressive and scalable equilibrium molecular sampling without strict invertibility constraints.
engineering_relevance: The approach can improve practical molecular simulation workflows by generating faster, high-quality equilibrium samples and supporting transferable models for larger biomolecular systems.
method: Use an autoregressive model to generate molecular configurations sequentially.
Retain Boltzmann Generator-style sampling with exact likelihoods and importance-sampling correction.
Train a large transferable model (Robin) to generalize across peptide systems.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports broad benchmark gains over flow-based models, with especially strong improvements on larger peptides such as 10-residue Chignolin and over 60% lower zero-shot energy error on 8-residue systems.
watch_item: Autoregressive sampling may introduce implementation and inference-time complexity, so performance and stability should be validated carefully on diverse molecular topologies.
